info.text:
"Full coverage" car insurance doesn't cover everything.

"Full coverage" has no official definition: it usually means liability + collision + comprehensive. Bankrate's 2026 national average: $2,697 a year.
A common state liability minimum is 25/50/25 ($25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash, $25,000 property). Bills above the limits aren't covered.
Usually not included: the loan gap, rental and towing unless added, wear and tear, rideshare driving.
Example: car worth $20,000, $25,000 loan, $500 deductible: payout $19,500, still owed $5,500. In 2023, 15.4% of drivers (about 1 in 7) were uninsured.

Sources: Bankrate (2026); West Virginia Insurance Commissioner; Insurance Research Council (2023 data); CNBC Select.
News and education, not financial advice.
